sections.html: Among the predatory tetras are the three or four species of Galeocharax. These fishes can reach a length of 20-25 cm. All species look very similar to each other; the determination is based mainly on the origin (Peru), as only G. gulo is reported from there so far.
These fishes are real rarities in the import business.

Galeocharax belong to the group of the so-called "water-dogs", which have needle-pointed teeth that are used to hold the prey. Such predators are only suited for specialized aquarists. They need large tanks as they are active swimmers. Against conspecifics the fish are relatively peaceful, as well as against tankmates that are too large to be eaten. However, Galeocharax are shy fish and this should be kept in mind with regard to planned tankmates.

Lexicon: Galeocharax: compound of the ancient Greek word for a small shark and "charax"; Charax is another genus of tetra. gulo: after the scientific name of the wolverine (Gulo gulo), the largest species of the weasel family.

Suggestion of a common name: Barrakuda water dog.
